text: A configuration version of the access panel of P4 is the triple of permission.matrix_version, masking_rule.masking_version and delegation_limit.limit_version over rows this service owns, with the valid_from and valid_to those rows carry, and no new table; the partner panel, the partner firm, the partner users and the fee schedule stay with S9 rwb-partner and FEAT-PRM-02 is not a prerequisite of this key; the effective-date bounds and the page bounds are parameter rows of rwb-case read through DP-06 with the version in force.
why: No source defines a configuration-version object, declares a publication operation, gives the matrix label a date column, or gives a value for the bounds, and the legacy key's panel name collides with the partner panel of S9.
read: Read the version as a label triple over permission, masking_rule and delegation_limit; read the two derived states from the rows' dates and the other five from the decision-record entry; read the bounds and the page limits through the parameters contract and hold no bound in code; read the partner panel as S9's and call it not at all.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access tech lead and the rwb-case tech lead before the two operations are frozen
impact: Fixes the two paths, the version identity, the state derivations and the bound names; changes no metadata value and adds no dependency

text: The effective date of a configuration version is resolved at read time by the own authorise operation as the version whose valid_from is on or before today and whose valid_to is after today, so the publication adds no Temporal Schedule, no workflow and no promotion job.
why: TSD P4 v3 T4 describes the lifecycle of a rule package version and no promotion job for an access-panel version, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access one Schedule only, the six-monthly access review list.
read: Read the version in force from the rows' dates at each authorise call and cache the answer; declare no Schedule and no workflow in the contract and add none to the rwb-access queue.
confirm: Solution architect and the Temporal platform owner at the contract review
impact: Keeps one Schedule on the rwb-access queue and makes the effective date data rather than a job; a later promotion job would be a new story

text: A publication is recorded as one entry of the local decision-record chain of DP-03 with the record code of a configuration publication, the three version labels, the effective date, the reason, the note, the publishing role code, the version superseded and the time, and the actor is held as a reference and never as a name, so no entry and no event carries a person.
why: No source gives the record code of a configuration publication, and the decision-record fields DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 carry references and no person field, while NFR-040 and Principle 5 forbid personal data in a shared record.
read: Append one entry per publication in the transaction that writes the dates, key it by versionId for the event, and carry role codes, labels, dates and reasons only.
confirm: Decision-record library owner and the data steward before the operations are frozen
impact: Fixes the entry content and the event payload; keeps personal data out of rwb.decision-record.v1 and rwb.access.events.v1

text: The QA sample is a three-part consistency check on the rule version recorded on each decision and on that version's rule row, and the service never re-evaluates a package.
why: The legacy criterion says 'tests each against the rule version that was in force' and the FSD repeats it, but no source says what the test is; the key's pattern list carries no DP-04 and no DP-08, so a Drools re-run is neither in scope nor possible.
read: For each sampled decision the service reads the rule version recorded on it through the P7 rule-model read and checks that its valid_from and valid_to cover the decision's decided_at, that the recorded rule_id is present in that version's rule_row set, and that the recorded answer agrees with that row's action_text and outputs; each item is PASS or FAIL with one reason code, and no package is evaluated, no KieBase is built and no decision is rewritten.
confirm: Confirm with the solution architect and the rwb-decision tech lead that the consistency reading is the target meaning, and with Internal audit that a FAIL verdict is an observation and not a re-decision.
impact: If the reading is rejected the story becomes a DP-04 story with an embedded Drools kit, a local package cache and a rule evaluator call, and its metadata, its dependencies and its test cases all change.

text: The default and maximum sample size, the period bounds, the page bounds, the draw rule and the reason-code set are parameter rows of rwb-case read through DP-06, never constants in code.
why: FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.1 BR-P4-024 says no value a business person may change is written in code, and the legacy story names no size, no bound and no code.
read: The parameters read of GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters answers the default and maximum sample size, the period bounds, the page bounds, the draw rule and the reason-code set at the version in force; a value outside its bound is a 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and a code outside the set is a configuration error and not a silent pass.
applied_in: RWB-P4-E8013-APP sections 3, 4, 5, 8 (BR6, BR10, BR11), 12.2, 13; RWB-P4-E8013-CON sections 7 (AC2, AC3), 11, 12.2
confirm: Confirm with the rwb-case owner that the parameter rows exist and are versioned, and with the conduct and QA officer that the sample size and the period bounds are business values and not design values.
impact: If a bound or a code is fixed in code, a change of sampling policy needs a release and the FSD measure of rule and limit changes without a code release cannot be met.

text: The run's entry is a DP-03 record carrying the run id, the period, the requested and drawn sizes, the passed and failed counts, the window and the reason code of each failure, with no person and no case narrative in it.
why: The legacy criterion requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version and NFR-040 limits each screen and each consumer to the personal data it needs, while no source states the field set of the run entry.
read: One entry is appended to the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library in the transaction that stores the answer and the stored items, it is hash-linked through prev_hash and entry_hash, it carries codes, counts, a window and times and no name, no e-mail address, no user reference and no case narrative, and the item set of the run is stored with it so a read never re-draws.
applied_in: RWB-P4-E8013-APP sections 1, 8 (BR8, BR9, BR13), 11, 12.3, 13, 17; RWB-P4-E8013-CON sections 7 (AC2), 11, 12.3, 12.7
confirm: Confirm with the decision-record library owner and with Internal audit that the counts and the per-failure reason codes are sufficient evidence of a run, and that no case narrative is needed in the record.
impact: If a narrative or a per-case outcome is required in the entry, the record grows a personal-data field, the NFR-040 review applies and the entry schema of the library is amended.
